archetype.name: Cup Contender (possession machine)
archetype.definition: A team that owns the puck and the shot clock so thoroughly that its record rests on process rather than percentages, and it has been built this way for years.

report.headline: Carolina's dominance is real: elite shot volume, ordinary luck, one goalie question.
report.take:
Carolina at 9-2-2 is not a hot start. It is the same team it has been for half a decade, with the dial turned up. The Hurricanes take 59% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts and 60% of the expected goals, second in the league in both. They lead the league with 33.9 shots on goal a game, 6.5 above the league average, and allow only 22.4, fourth-fewest. History says this is the franchise's natural state. CF % has sat at 0.59 or 0.60 in every season on the sheet, and last year ended with 16 playoff wins, a Cup run. The site ranks them second, and the Goal Diff / GP of 1.38, also second, says the record has been earned.

The important part is what is not producing the results. The 5-on-5 PDO is 99.7, slightly below average. The all-situations version, 100.6, sits exactly on the league mark. Shooting % is .116, 14th in the league, barely above average. Pts vs Goal Diff is 0.2, so there is no bank of fluky one-goal or overtime wins either. Carolina is winning by outshooting people badly and converting at a normal rate. That is the most repeatable way to win in hockey. Both special teams add to it, with the PP % at .255 and the PK % at .837, each roughly four to five points better than the league.

The depth makes the grades credible. Forwards and blueline are both A+, and neither grade leans on one player. Svechnikov ranks 3rd among right wings on his tab, Blake 7th, Aho 6th of 230 centers and Stankoven 8th. On the back end Gostisbehere ranks 3rd of 250 defensemen and Walker 12th. Every regular forward and defenseman is above a 51% expected-goals share, and most are near or above 60%. Aho drives the scoring with 18 points. Blake has just 2 goals on 38 shots, so some finishing is still owed to him.

The one soft spot is the net. Goaltending grades a C, and team GSAx is 0.4, 19th. That average hides a real split. Kochetkov is at .916 with +4.4 GSAx over 7 starts, while Bussi is at .865 with -4.6 over 6. Carolina has won anyway, which shows how much the skaters cover. But the gap between this team and a runaway Presidents' Trophy pace mostly comes down to who starts in goal.

strengths.title: Shot volume nobody else matches
strengths.body: Carolina leads the league in shots on goal a game and ranks near the top in fewest allowed. Its 5-on-5 shot-attempt and expected-goal shares are both second. This is structural: the same CF % has shown up every season on the sheet. It is the most durable edge a team can have.

strengths.title: Results without the luck
strengths.body: The Goal Diff / GP of 1.38 comes with a below-average 5-on-5 PDO and near-zero Pts vs Goal Diff. Nothing in the record is propped up by hot shooting or coin-flip overtime wins. If anything, the percentages have room to rise.

strengths.title: Deep, A+ skater groups
strengths.body: Four forwards rank in the top eight at their positions. Gostisbehere ranks third among all defensemen and carries a big share of the power play. Because the grades are spread across the lineup, an injury or slump to one player would not break the group.

concerns.title: A goaltending split, not a tandem
concerns.body: Kochetkov has been well above average, and Bussi has given back more than Kochetkov has saved. That leaves the team GSAx near zero and the group grade at C. Shots against are low, so the damage stays contained. But in tighter games, a Bussi start is the likeliest way this team loses.

concerns.title: Opposing centers are getting through
concerns.body: The defense holds wingers and defensemen well under their expected points. Centers, though, are scoring above theirs, and they take a far larger share of the points against than the league norm. Thirteen games is a small sample, but it hints that the middle of the ice is the leak in an otherwise airtight structure.

concerns.title: Slightly looser lately
concerns.body: The last five games, mostly on the road, came in at 3-1-1. Carolina allowed 2.8 a game in that stretch, a bit worse than its season rate, and that included a 6-5 overtime loss in Edmonton. That is minor drift rather than a trend, and a homestand should help.

trend.note: After an opening loss came a 7-game winning streak and an 8-1-1 run over the last ten. The last five were a touch less dominant on a long road swing, but the underlying shot and chance shares have never wavered.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games, and Boston's hot percentages meet Carolina's process.
weekAhead.body:
After a heavy road stretch, Carolina gets three straight at home. Boston, the site's top team, comes in first, then two struggling sides in Columbus and Winnipeg. The Bruins are the week's real test, and the matchup is a near-perfect contrast. Boston's league-best goal differential sits on a 107.6 PDO and a league-leading GSAx of 10.9. Its shot-attempt share is under 50%, and it is outshot most nights. Carolina will likely control the puck. The question is whether it can beat a goalie group that has stopped nearly everything.

Columbus and Winnipeg should be wins. The Blue Jackets' PK % is .710, 24th in the league, which plays straight into Carolina's power play. Winnipeg scores little, ranking 27th on offense with a .084 Shooting %, and it allows plenty of shots. Its A- goaltending is the only thing keeping games close. Carolina already beat the Jets 3-2 in Winnipeg this month, and that kind of game is the likely shape again.

keyMatchups.title: Process vs. percentages against Boston
keyMatchups.body: Boston shoots .152 and saves .925, both second in the league, while ranking 17th in shot-attempt share. That mix tends to cool over a season, but it can win any single night. Boston also holds forwards furthest under their expected points of any team but one, so Carolina's depth scoring may need to come from the blueline.

keyMatchups.title: Carolina power play vs. Columbus PK
keyMatchups.body: Carolina's power play converts well above the league rate, and Columbus kills penalties at one of the league's worst rates. With the Blue Jackets also 28th on offense, a couple of power-play goals could settle this one early.

keyMatchups.title: Volume against Winnipeg's goalies
keyMatchups.body: The Jets allow 29.1 shots a game, 25th in the league, and give defensemen more points than expected. That suits Gostisbehere and Walker. Winnipeg's goalies rank seventh in GSAx, so Carolina may need its usual barrage just to break through.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in goal against Boston: Kochetkov makes it a coin flip Carolina should win on process, while a Bussi start tilts it toward the Bruins' hot finishing.

restOfSeason.body:
The 126-point pace will not hold, since nobody sustains a .750 start. But very little here is luck to give back. The percentages are average, close-game luck is neutral, and the shot and chance shares match what this franchise has produced for years. That points to a high floor. Expect the usual 110-plus-point Carolina season, a division title as the most likely outcome, and scoring that eases back from the October burst toward the high-3s a game as the schedule evens out.

The upside lever is goaltending. If Kochetkov takes most of the starts and keeps saving above expected, the C grade rises and this becomes the league's best team on paper and in the standings. If the split continues, Carolina still wins most nights but loses a few games that elite possession should have banked.
swingFactors: Kochetkov's share of starts and Bussi's save %
Whether the leak against opposing centers closes
Skater health given how much depth drives the A+ grades

confidence.note: Only 13 games, but the process numbers match years of history.
